articleHeadline: Trivalent Antiviral Conjugates Trap Influenza Viruses by Cross-Linking Them
articleSummary: Influenza antiviral strategy expanded with multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) tethered to an Fc fragment, developed by researchers from the Academy of Military Medical Sciences in Beijing with Tsinghua University, Xiamen University and the University of Hong Kong. Using click chemistry, the team built mono-, di-, and tri-valent zanamivir-Fc (AVC-Z1–Z3) and a tri-valent peramivir-Fc (AVC-P3). Tri-valent AVC-Z3 showed superior antiviral activity and, crucially, induced inter-virion aggregation by cross-linking neuraminidase-bearing virions, producing a dual-stage inhibition that blocks both entry and release. AVC-P3 displayed stronger in vitro activity and a longer in vivo half-life than AVC-Z3 and CD388 with YTE. In mouse models challenged with H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, and influenza B, AVC-P3 outperformed other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388, suggesting broad, long-acting prophylactic/therapeutic potential against diverse influenza A and B threats.

articleHeadline: Continuing mumps outbreak in Keralam leads to renewed demand for MMR vaccine
articleSummary: Mumps outbreak in Keralam ongoing since late 2023 persists into 2026, with 74,907 cases in 2024, 26,462 in 2025, and 6,606 cases so far in 2026. articleSummary: Kissing bugs (Triatominae), vectors of the parasite causing Chagas disease, spread across the Americas in three major waves over ~60 million years, with dispersal tied to global paleotemperatures. Climate shifts (warm Paleocene–Eocene, cooler Oligocene, Miocene–Pleistocene fluctuations) coincide with the pattern, illuminating the historical reach of Chagas disease vectors.

articleSummary: Pune has recorded 2,009 suspected dengue cases this year, with about 66% reported in August–October (484 in August, 508 in September, 346 in October). The Pune Municipal Corporation found 2,651 mosquito breeding sites across homes, societies, offices and colleges, with water stored at residences and construction sites fueling vector propagation. Dengue is now a year‑round urban threat in Pune, driven by environmental and human factors that sustain transmission beyond the monsoon. Aedes aegypti breeds in small pockets of clean, stagnant water inside and around homes; coolers, flowerpots and discarded tyres provide constant breeding sites. articleSummary: Hepatitis B risk among healthcare workers in Kumasi, Ghana, was highlighted in a cross-sectional study of 625 staff across four hospitals (Nov–Dec 2023), published in BMC Health Services Research. Limitations include purposive sampling and cross‑sectional design, potentially limiting generalizability to the Ashanti Region.

articleHeadline: Brazil Syphilis Hotspots Expand Along Atlantic Coast
articleSummary: Gestational syphilis and congenital syphilis in Brazil expanded along the Atlantic coast, with a 2011–2022 spatiotemporal analysis using the Brazilian Unified Health System data. articleSummary: Salmonella group D caused purulent meningitis with sepsis in a 13‑month‑old girl in Weifang, Shandong, China. articleSummary: As of 2026-10-18, researchers at Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya, India, published in Discover Artificial Intelligence a study introducing a two-hidden-layer neural network (TLNN) to emulate a nonlinear anthrax infection model in animals. articleSummary: As of 2026-10-18, researchers from IRD, CNRS, University of Montpellier (France) and Mahidol University (Thailand) report that saliva from infected mosquitoes carries a viral RNA fragment (sfRNA) that promotes infection by suppressing the host's initial innate immune response at the bite site. articleSummary: Ebola and Marburg are highly dangerous hemorrhagic fevers caused by filoviruses in the Filoviridae family. In 2023, Equatorial Guinea reported a Marburg outbreak with nine deaths and sixteen suspected cases. Transmission is through contact with infected animals or body fluids; airborne spread is not typical. Incubation is 2–21 days; prevention focuses on minimizing exposure, rapid case identification, isolation, contact tracing, and safe burial practices. CFR: Ebola ~50%; Marburg 24–90%.
